key_insight: LCGuard is a lightweight latent communication guard that selectively sanitizes transformer KV-cache sharing between agents, preserving task-relevant signals while preventing leakage of contextual, intermediate, or agent-specific information.
problem_solved: Enables safe latent (KV) communication in LLM-based multi-agent systems by addressing the risk that shared KV caches leak sensitive contextual inputs and opaque internal reasoning states, for which no practical control mechanism previously existed.
method: Policy-aware KV filtering: operate directly on transformer key/value caches to mask or suppress components likely to reveal private or irrelevant information while retaining task-critical content.
Learned gating with utility-leakage trade-off: train a lightweight plug-in module (with regularizers or auxiliary discriminators) that optimizes performance under explicit leakage constraints.
Model-agnostic, low-overhead integration: designed as a compatibility layer for existing transformer-based agents to impose runtime controls on KV sharing with minimal latency/compute cost.
impact: Allows practitioners to exploit efficient, information-rich latent communication channels without sacrificing privacy or controllability, making multi-agent LLM deployments safer and more trustworthy for real-world, sensitive applications.
visual_elements: System diagram: multiple agent boxes with KV arrows between them and an LCGuard filter icon on each channel
Before vs after chart: leakage risk (high) vs task performance plotted before LCGuard and after LCGuard (reduced leakage, maintained performance)
KV cache illustration: vector/table with highlighted dimensions that are masked/filtered
Pipeline flowchart: detect sensitive latent components → apply filter/gate → share sanitized KV
paper_title: LCGuard: Latent Communication Guard for Safe KV Sharing in Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Sadia Asif, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Momin Abbas, Prasanna Sattigeri, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy
